mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives lower equity prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE > 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST over two months indicates supply chain normalization with reduced housing demand pressure, which boosts corporate margins and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% MoM and HOUST < 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth signals an emergency monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.5% in one month AND GDPC1 YoY < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls sharply and GDP is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals rising consumer savings and precautionary behavior, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently above its 12-month moving average for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and UNRATE above 6% for two months indicates robust labor market expansion, which increases wage growth and inflation, ultimately raising discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0% MoM and UNRATE > 6% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed thresholds for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in HOUST for six consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which reduces construction and related spending, lowering GDP growth expectations and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 0% MoM for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls for six consecutive months.
